summary: Reorganized the growth section so its assumptions and scenario indicators lead directly into stage gates informed by the modeled break-even and capacity results.

replies.reply: I agree with this restructuring. The current section asks the reader to interpret the stages before seeing the assumptions and scenario results that should govern them. The proposed structure is planning basis, scenario indicators, and then stage gates. It also makes the main outputs directly comparable and shows what each stage is intended to prove. Because reordering and restructuring both tables are interdependent, I have kept the change atomic.

patch_proposals.original_text:
The growth plan should be staged. Crust Chant should not promise guaranteed projections before real customer data exists. The company should instead use scenarios and decision gates. The numbers below are illustrative planning ranges only and should be replaced by actual sales and cost data after launch.

| **Stage / scenario**        | **Practical meaning**                                                                                             | **Indicative scale to test**                                                                     | **Decision focus**                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stage 1: Controlled launch  | Small order windows, limited SKUs, direct retail first, small wholesale samples only.                             | Roughly 20-50 bread-unit equivalents per week, depending on production schedule and demand.      | Can the company produce, deliver, collect payment, and receive useful feedback without chaos? |
| Stage 2: Repeat-demand base | Clear weekly rhythm, growing repeat customers, first subscription trials, carefully selected wholesale.           | Roughly 60-150 bread-unit equivalents per week plus selected wholesale tests.                    | Which products/channels create repeat demand with acceptable delivery and labor cost?         |
| Stage 3: Operational growth | More order windows or production days, route density improves, helper/rider support becomes justified.            | Roughly 150-300 bread-unit equivalents per week if demand and production remain stable.          | Does added volume improve economics or create quality/service problems?                       |
| Stage 4: Expansion option   | Larger production rhythm, more staff, stronger wholesale/subscription base, possible facility/capacity decisions. | Above 300 bread-unit equivalents per week only after proven repeat demand and capacity planning. | Is expansion justified by repeat demand, margin, cash flow, and founder workload?             |

| **Planning component**                  | **Definition, provisional value, and use**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Break-even definition                   | Break-even is reached when contribution from sales covers all recurring fixed operating costs, including the director salary, leaving neither an operating profit nor an operating loss. Report both the required monthly sale units and the retail/wholesale quantities used to reach them. The first 3–6 months should validate whether actual demand, selling prices, discounts, product mix, and operating costs support the scenario.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Verified contribution inputs            | The internal *Crust Chant Provisional Break-even Analysis*—a read-only repository and database audit completed 29 July 2026—found approximately **138 THB contribution per ordinary direct-retail sale unit**, **33 THB per wholesale sale unit**, and **7,622 THB/month in the audited fixed-cost proxy**. The proxy comprises approximately **7,054 THB/month of straight-line depreciation for 11 active equipment records with complete inputs** and **568 THB/month of fixed refrigeration electricity**. Because the equipment is personally owned and is intended to be leased to Crust Chant, the depreciation amount is only a temporary placeholder for the company's equipment cost. The final management model should replace it with the gross monthly equipment rent and must not count both rent and depreciation for the same assets. A twelfth active record, the Air Conditioner, lacked complete depreciation inputs and was excluded rather than assigned a zero cost. Contribution is the amount left after verified direct product costs, including recipe-level production labor. It pays monthly company expenses and director salary before company profit. One ordinary retail unit therefore contributes about as much as 4.2 wholesale units. Low-Salt Country Blonde is excluded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| How labor costs are counted                    | Recipe-level production labor remains inside each product's variable unit cost as the cost of making the bread. The gross director salary is counted separately as a recurring monthly company expense. This intentionally conservative treatment may overstate the initial cash requirement if the director personally performs both production and management work, but it avoids a long-term model that assumes production labor is free. No additional owner-income target is added.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Initial channel-mix assumption              | Use **40% ordinary direct retail / 60% wholesale by sale units** as an initial planning scenario. This gives approximately **75 THB weighted contribution per unit**. It is not a demand forecast. Subscription units must use their own contribution rather than being silently treated as ordinary retail, and the pilot's wholesale-dominated mix is historical evidence rather than the target.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Plausible 35,000 THB salary case        | Before the equipment rent and Thai-employee compensation are finalized, monthly cost to cover is **39,943 THB + E + T**, where `E` is the gross monthly rent paid by Crust Chant for the founder-owned equipment and `T` is the four Thai employees' monthly compensation not already included in verified product or channel unit costs: 568 THB fixed refrigeration electricity + 35,000 THB gross director salary + up to 875 THB employer social security for the director + up to 3,500 THB total employer social security for four Thai employees + `E` + `T`. If `E` is provisionally set at **7,054 THB** and `T` is zero because all employee pay is already captured in the contribution inputs, total monthly cost is **46,997 THB**. At the 40/60 mix, this requires approximately **627 units/month or 145/week: 251 retail and 376 wholesale**. At a 50/50 mix, it requires approximately **550 units/month or 127/week: 275 retail and 275 wholesale**. Recalculate these quantities when the gross rent, actual employee compensation, and insurable wages are finalized.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Conservative 50,000 THB salary case     | Before the equipment rent and Thai-employee compensation are finalized, monthly cost to cover is **54,943 THB + E + T**, where `E` is the gross monthly rent paid by Crust Chant for the founder-owned equipment and `T` is the four Thai employees' monthly compensation not already included in verified product or channel unit costs: 568 THB fixed refrigeration electricity + 50,000 THB gross director salary + up to 875 THB employer social security for the director + up to 3,500 THB total employer social security for four Thai employees + `E` + `T`. If `E` is provisionally set at **7,054 THB** and `T` is zero because all employee pay is already captured in the contribution inputs, total monthly cost is **61,997 THB**. At the 40/60 mix, this requires approximately **827 units/month or 191/week: 331 retail and 496 wholesale**. At a 50/50 mix, it requires approximately **726 units/month or 168/week: 363 retail and 363 wholesale**. Recalculate these quantities when the gross rent, actual employee compensation, and insurable wages are finalized.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Production-capacity feasibility check | The demonstrated baseline is **50 loaves in one two-day production cycle**. Refrigeration for dough retardation is currently the main equipment constraint and can hold approximately **70–80 loaves**. With controlled dough temperature and timely shaping and retardation, use **70–80 loaves per two-day cycle** as the provisional committed capacity. Assuming for this comparison that one modeled sale unit corresponds to one loaf requiring similar refrigeration space, the recalculated 35,000 THB scenarios requiring 127–145 units/week need **two cycles or approximately four production days/week**, providing capacity for 140–160 loaves. The 145-unit case requires an average of at least approximately 73 loaves per cycle and therefore exceeds the lower 70-loaf commitment boundary. The 50,000 THB scenarios requiring 168–191 units/week should use **three cycles or approximately six production days/week**, providing capacity for 210–240 loaves. Any Thai-employee compensation represented by `T` rather than already included in unit contribution would increase these volume and capacity requirements. |
| Profit indicator above break-even       | At the 40/60 mix, each additional 100 sale units per month—40 retail and 60 wholesale—adds approximately **7,500 THB of contribution** before omitted costs and tax. At a 50/50 mix, each additional 100 units adds approximately **8,550 THB**. These increments become company profit only after every operating cost, including production labor and director salary, is covered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
patch_proposals.suggested_text:
The growth plan starts with the assumptions and indicators used in the current scenarios, then converts those results into stage gates. Crust Chant should not treat the figures as guaranteed projections: actual selling prices, product and channel mix, demand, costs, capacity, and founder workload must replace the provisional inputs after launch.

### Planning basis

| **Planning component** | **Current basis** | **Indicator or management use** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Break-even definition | Contribution from sales covers all recurring fixed operating costs, including the director salary, leaving neither operating profit nor operating loss. The first 3–6 months are a validation period. | Track required monthly and weekly sale units, retail and wholesale quantities, actual contribution, and the gap to break-even. |
| Verified contribution inputs | The internal *Crust Chant Provisional Break-even Analysis*—a read-only repository and database audit completed 29 July 2026—found approximately **138 THB contribution per ordinary direct-retail sale unit** and **33 THB per wholesale sale unit** after verified direct product costs, including recipe-level production labour. One ordinary retail unit therefore contributes about as much as 4.2 wholesale units. Low-Salt Country Blonde is excluded. | Recalculate contribution from actual selling prices, discounts, product mix, and direct costs. Subscription units must use their own contribution. |
| Fixed operating-cost base | Fixed refrigeration electricity is **568 THB/month**. The audited equipment proxy is **7,054 THB/month** of straight-line depreciation for 11 active equipment records with complete inputs. A twelfth active record, the Air Conditioner, lacked complete inputs and was excluded rather than assigned zero. Because the equipment is personally owned and intended to be leased to Crust Chant, gross equipment rent `E` must replace the depreciation placeholder without counting both. | Finalize `E`; verify the missing equipment input; add every omitted recurring company cost before treating a scenario as a full break-even target. |
| Labour and salary treatment | Recipe-level production labour remains in variable unit cost. Gross director salary is a recurring fixed company expense, with no additional owner-income target. Four Thai employees' compensation must be included in product or channel unit costs or in monthly variable `T`, but not both. Employer social security is modeled separately. | Verify actual employee compensation, its location in the cost model, and insurable wages; then replace `T` and the conservative contribution caps. |
| Channel-mix scenarios | The initial case uses **40% ordinary direct retail / 60% wholesale by sale units**, giving approximately **75 THB weighted contribution per unit**. A comparison case uses **50% / 50%**, giving approximately **85.50 THB per unit**. Neither is a demand forecast, and the pilot's wholesale-dominated mix is historical evidence rather than the target. | Compare actual unit mix and weighted contribution with both cases; do not silently classify subscription units as ordinary retail. |
| Capacity basis | The demonstrated baseline is **50 loaves in one two-day production cycle**. Refrigeration is the main current constraint. Provisional committed capacity is **70–80 loaves per two-day cycle**, or 140–160 across two cycles and 210–240 across three cycles. | Compare weekly demand with the lower and upper capacity boundaries, then verify product-level space and labour rather than assuming every sale unit is physically identical. |
| Profit above break-even | After every operating cost is covered, an additional 100 monthly sale units add approximately **7,500 THB** at the 40/60 mix or **8,550 THB** at the 50/50 mix, before omitted costs and tax. | Track contribution above the verified break-even point; do not label it profit while costs remain omitted. |

### Scenario indicators

| **Indicator** | **35,000 THB salary, 40/60 mix** | **35,000 THB salary, 50/50 mix** | **50,000 THB salary, 40/60 mix** | **50,000 THB salary, 50/50 mix** |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Weighted contribution per sale unit | 75 THB | 85.50 THB | 75 THB | 85.50 THB |
| Monthly cost to cover with `E = 7,054 THB` and `T = 0` | 46,997 THB | 46,997 THB | 61,997 THB | 61,997 THB |
| Required total sale units per month | 627 | 550 | 827 | 726 |
| Required total sale units per week | 145 | 127 | 191 | 168 |
| Required retail / wholesale units per month | 251 / 376 | 275 / 275 | 331 / 496 | 363 / 363 |
| Provisional production commitment | 2 cycles, about 4 production days/week | 2 cycles, about 4 production days/week | 3 cycles, about 6 production days/week | 3 cycles, about 6 production days/week |
| Committed weekly capacity used for comparison | 140–160 loaves | 140–160 loaves | 210–240 loaves | 210–240 loaves |
| Capacity headroom against modeled weekly units | **5-unit shortfall** at 140; 15-unit buffer at 160 | 13–33-unit buffer | 19–49-unit buffer | 42–72-unit buffer |
| Contribution from 100 additional monthly units | 7,500 THB | 8,550 THB | 7,500 THB | 8,550 THB |

Here, `E` is gross monthly equipment rent and `T` is Thai-employee compensation not already included in verified product or channel unit costs. Setting `E` to 7,054 THB and `T` to zero is only a comparison case, not a conclusion that the final values will equal those amounts. Capacity comparisons provisionally treat one modeled sale unit as one loaf requiring similar refrigeration space.

### Stage gates informed by the scenarios

| **Stage / scenario** | **Operating objective** | **Indicative scale to test** | **Learning carried from the scenarios** | **Decision gate** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stage 1: Controlled launch | Run small order windows, limited SKUs, direct retail first, and small wholesale samples. | Roughly 20–50 sale units/week, subject to product-level capacity conversion. | This is deliberately below either modeled salary break-even range. Its purpose is to replace provisional contribution, cost, mix, and workload assumptions with observed data. | Can the company produce, deliver, collect payment, and capture reliable unit economics and customer feedback without operational chaos? |
| Stage 2: Repeat-demand base | Establish a clear weekly rhythm, repeat customers, first subscription trials, and carefully selected wholesale. | Roughly 60–150 sale units/week. | The modeled 35,000 THB salary cases require **127–145 units/week**. Two cycles provide 140–160 loaves of provisional capacity, but the 145-unit case exceeds the lower 140-loaf boundary and needs at least about 73 loaves per cycle. | Does repeat demand support the required channel mix and contribution while two weekly production cycles remain reliable and founder workload stays acceptable? |
| Stage 3: Operational break-even and growth | Add order windows or production days only after repeat demand and route density justify the workload. | Roughly 150–300 sale units/week. | The modeled 50,000 THB salary cases require **168–191 units/week** and should use three cycles, or about six production days/week. This may achieve modeled break-even but leaves little weekly recovery time and still excludes unresolved costs. | Can the company sustain three cycles, quality, fulfilment, delivery, staffing, and verified full-cost break-even without making the operation fragile? |
| Stage 4: Expansion option | Consider larger production rhythm, more staff, stronger wholesale or subscription channels, and facility or refrigeration changes. | Above 300 sale units/week only after demand and capacity are proven. | Current modeled salary break-even ranges fall below this stage; expansion should therefore be justified by durable demand, margin, cash flow, capacity, and workload rather than by the salary threshold alone. | Does observed demand justify capital or fixed-cost expansion, and does the added scale improve profit and resilience rather than merely increase activity? |
patch_proposals.reason: This makes the reasoning sequence explicit: define the planning model, compare its decision indicators, and use those outputs to set stage-specific learning and operating gates. One atomic replacement is required because both complete tables are structurally changed and reordered.
patch_proposals.risk: The new tables are easier to scan but remain provisional. Their capacity rows still use the simplifying assumption that one modeled sale unit corresponds to one loaf with similar refrigeration needs, and the cost scenarios still exclude unresolved employee compensation and other omitted costs. The detailed calculation references and limitations below the tables remain unchanged.
